Under Sudan's Muslim Personal Status Act of 1991, young children stay with their mother after a divorce, and custody passes to the father when a son turns 7 and a daughter 9. Guardianship and the children's support stay with the father (OECD SIGI 2019)
Where Islamic family law applies, young children usually stay with their mother while legal guardianship often stays with the father. Where children grow up varies widely by country and family custom
In South Asia the father is often seen as the legal guardian, but young children usually stay with their mother (India's Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act: usually the mother until age five)
In much of Africa custom says children belong to the father's family, yet more of them actually live with their mother
In Korea about 78% of single parents aged 20 to 39 raising children alone are mothers (Statistics Korea, young single-parent households 2023)

In Japan about 85% of divorcing couples give the mother parental authority over all the children (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Vital Statistics). From April 2026 couples can also choose joint parental authority

In the US about 80% of custodial parents of children whose parents live apart are mothers (US Census Bureau 2020)
Of Canadian children whose parents separated, about 70% live mainly with their mother, 15% with their father, and 9% split their time equally (Statistics Canada 2011)

Children whose parents separate mostly live with their mother. In Canada and the US 70-80% live mainly with their mother, one or two in ten with their father, and the rest move between two homes (Statistics Canada 2011, US Census Bureau 2020)
